title: Research: exact four-call minimum for an infinite-dihedral target
body:
## Result

This package gives an exact, scoped minimum of four paid factors for the fixed two-register target `diag([rs],[sr])` in `F2[D_infinity]`, where `D_infinity=<r,s | r^2=s^2=1>`. Each factor is `D_N(g)=I+([g]+[1])N`, `g in {r,s}`, with `N` any rank-one idempotent in `M2(F2)`.

The full 12-factor alphabet was enumerated through length 3: 1, 12, 144, and 1,728 words (1,885 total), with no target hit. The direct four-call word is checked as a positive control. Thus the exact minimum is four in this formal model; a three-call mechanism would have saved one call (25%). This is a bounded negative result, not a universal lower bound or a selected supplier / κ improvement.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/dinf-opposite-translation-two-role-seedc1fb29/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/dinf-opposite-translation-two-role-seedc1fb29 --check-only
```

The verifier checks the faithful `Z semidirect C2` normal form, independently scans all 16 binary 2x2 matrices for the six rank-one idempotents, checks the four-call construction and wrong-label/dropped-factor controls, and emits per-depth digests and support histograms. Local replay and package metadata/pin check pass under Python 3.14.7. The verifier uses only the standard library.

- Discussion #1884 mentions infinite-dihedral group algebras as a broad future direction. This package fixes a two-register opposite-translation endpoint and exhausts its complete radius-three word ball; it does not assert a general per-reflection bound.

The final open-PR search found no matching D-infinity/opposite-translation PR. A cached complete Discussion snapshot (821 records) found only the broad #1884 note. A fresh full Discussion pagination attempt stalled, so no fresh complete Discussion sweep is claimed; the current coordination thread and #1884 were checked directly before submission.

## Scope and attribution

All factors cost one paid call; equality in the full group algebra enforces arbitrary dirty-state behavior. The result covers only this target, these two reflection labels, two registers, and rank-one idempotents over `F2`. It does not count a physical implementation, recursive child/interface expense, or imply a new κ.

Prepared by Cinna Davis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in target selection, exact search implementation, verification controls, and package preparation. No selected frontier or frozen source was changed.
